baseFrontend: validated v84 runtime with NexoWatt EOS role, first-login and product branding hardening
label: v87-rc2
notes: Stable 7.9.86 remains unchanged; this release candidate becomes 7.9.87 stable only after system and field acceptance.
Administrator/NexoWatt Service keeps unrestricted access and is never forced through first-login password setup.
Installer and end-user accounts must choose their own password at the first authenticated login.
Installers receive commissioning and troubleshooting access without users, credentials, repositories, certificates, ACL or expert administration.
End users can open EOS Admin for Smart Home, room/function assignment and explicitly released NexoWatt UI surfaces.
Customer-visible platform branding is NexoWatt EOS; technical compatibility identifiers and third-party license notices remain internal.
After first-login password setup, every detected authentication-session representation is invalidated server-side and authentication cookies are cleared.
changes: Creates and repairs NexoWatt Service, Installer and End User role groups with purpose-specific ACL profiles.
Repairs EOS Admin, system configuration and repository metadata ACLs so authenticated installer/end-user sessions can read the shell without gaining direct system-write access.
Keeps certificates, platform licenses and credential objects restricted to NexoWatt Admin / Service.
Adds a blocking first-login password workflow for installer/end-user roles with server-side password validation and forced logout.
Allows end-user Smart Home room/function assignments while keeping raw system, adapter and expert areas hidden.
Adds a low-overhead visible-branding sanitizer for NexoWatt EOS product presentation.
Uses the authenticated EOS self-service route with trusted backend context so installer/end-user roles can set their own first-login password without global user-management rights.
Fails closed to the end-user policy for missing socket identities and invalidates first-login sessions after the password is changed.
